title: ConcurrentHashMap internals — Java 7 segments vs Java 8 CAS + per-bucket sync + treeify

s1_definition.profdef: **Java 7 CHM**: array of 16 **Segments**, each a mini-HashMap with its own lock. Concurrency level = 16 (16 threads can write to 16 different segments simultaneously). Limitation: fixed segment count, entire segment locked for write. **Java 8+ CHM**: NO segments. Uses a flat `Node[] table` (like HashMap). **Reads**: completely lock-free using `volatile` reads. **Writes**: CAS (Compare-And-Swap) for inserting into empty bucket, `synchronized` on the FIRST NODE of the bucket for inserting into non-empty bucket. Only the specific bucket is locked — other buckets remain accessible. **Treeify**: same as HashMap (threshold 8). **Distributed resize**: multiple threads help resize concurrently using `transferIndex` — each thread claims a chunk of buckets to migrate.
s1_definition.analogy: **Java 7**: bank with 16 SECTIONS, each with its own lock. Two people in section 1? One waits. But sections 2-16 are free. **Java 8**: bank with NO sections — each individual drawer has its own lock. Two people at different drawers? Both proceed. Lock only when two people touch the SAME drawer. Reading a drawer? NO lock needed (just peek through the glass). Expanding the cabinet? ALL employees help simultaneously — each takes a chunk of drawers to migrate.
s1_definition.oneliner: Java 7: 16 segment locks. Java 8: CAS for empty buckets + synchronized per-bucket + lock-free reads + concurrent resize. Much finer granularity.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** **Java 7 CHM**: array of 16 **Segments**, each a mini-HashMap with its own lock. Concurrency level = 16 (16 threads can write to 16 different segments simultaneously). Limitation: fixed segment count, entire segment locked for write. **Java 8+ CHM**: NO segments. Uses a flat `Node[] table` (like HashMap). **Reads**: completely lock-free using `volatile` reads. **Writes**: CAS (Compare-And-Swap) for inserting into empty bucket, `synchronized` on the FIRST NODE of the bucket for inserting into non-empty bucket. Only the specific bucket is locked — other buckets remain accessible. **Treeify**: same as HashMap (threshold 8). **Distributed resize**: multiple threads help resize concurrently using `transferIndex` — each thread claims a chunk of buckets to migrate.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **Java 7**: bank with 16 SECTIONS, each with its own lock. Two people in section 1? One waits. But sections 2-16 are free. **Java 8**: bank with NO sections — each individual drawer has its own lock. Two people at different drawers? Both proceed. Lock only when two people touch the SAME drawer. Reading a drawer? NO lock needed (just peek through the glass). Expanding the cabinet? ALL employees help simultaneously — each takes a chunk of drawers to migrate.

**One line to remember:** Java 7: 16 segment locks. Java 8: CAS for empty buckets + synchronized per-bucket + lock-free reads + concurrent resize. Much finer granularity.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The real-time trade cache on Java 7 had 16 segments.** With 64 cores, only 16 concurrent writes were possible — 48 cores waited. During market open (spike): 500K writes/sec bottlenecked on 16 segment locks. Fix: upgraded to Java 8+ CHM — per-bucket locking with CAS for empty buckets. With 64K buckets: virtually no contention. Throughput: 500K → 2M writes/sec. Resize during growth: distributed across all threads — no single-thread bottleneck.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is many threads updating account balances in a `ConcurrentHashMap` at the same time.

**Step 1.** A thread updating Rajesh's bucket uses a CAS (compare-and-swap) to place the first node in an empty bucket without any lock.

**Step 2.** If that bucket already has entries, the thread synchronizes only on that single bucket's head node, so updates to Priya's bucket proceed in parallel.

**Step 3.** When a bucket's chain grows past the threshold it is treeified for faster lookups, and all threads see a consistent map without the global locking that the old Java 7 segment design required.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ JAVA 7: Segment Locking ═══

  Segment[0]  Segment[1] ... Segment[15]
  [lock][map] [lock][map]    [lock][map]
  Thread-1 →  Thread-2  →    Thread-16 → simultaneous!
  Thread-17 WAITS for Segment[0] lock!

  ═══ JAVA 8: Per-Bucket CAS + Sync ═══

  Node[] table:
  [0][1][2][3][4][5][6]...[N]
   ↑  ↑  ↑
   T1 T2 T3 → ALL write simultaneously (different buckets)!

  Empty bucket → CAS (lock-free!)
  Non-empty bucket → synchronized(firstNode) — only THIS bucket locked!
  Read → ALWAYS lock-free (volatile)!

  ═══ CONCURRENT RESIZE ═══
  Thread-1: migrates buckets 0-15    ←┐
  Thread-2: migrates buckets 16-31   ← parallel!
  Thread-3: migrates buckets 32-47   ←┘
  N threads = N times faster resize!
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  Real-Time Balance Cache (ConcurrentHashMap)
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  N payment threads (concurrent updates)      │
  └──────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                 ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ ConcurrentHashMap<AcctId, Balance>        │
   │  reads: lock-free (volatile)              │
   │  writes: CAS empty / sync per-bucket      │
   │  computeIfAbsent: atomic, runs ONCE       │
   └──────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                  ▼
        2M ops/sec (per-bucket granularity)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Java 7 ConcurrentHashMap used 16 Segments — each a mini-HashMap with its own lock. Maximum 16 concurrent writes. Java 8+ redesigned completely: flat `Node[]` table (no segments), reads are 100% lock-free (volatile reads), writes use CAS for empty buckets (no lock at all) and `synchronized` on the first node of non-empty buckets (only that bucket locked). This gives per-bucket granularity — with 64K buckets, 64K concurrent writes are theoretically possible.

Java 8+ also introduced: treeification (same as HashMap — threshold 8), and distributed resize where multiple threads help migrate buckets concurrently (each claims a stride via CAS on `transferIndex`). `computeIfAbsent` is atomic — even with 10 threads calling simultaneously, the compute function executes exactly ONCE. No null keys/values allowed (ambiguity in concurrent context: does null mean "absent" or "mapped to null"?). In banking: real-time balance cache — Java 7 CHM with 16 segments: 500K ops/sec. Java 8+ CHM with per-bucket locking: 2M ops/sec. 4x improvement from finer granularity.

---

keyPoints: Java 7: segment-based locking (16 segments by default)
Java 8+: CAS + per-bucket synchronized — finer granularity
Reads never block — volatile reads of node values
size() is approximate under concurrency — use mappingCount() for long
